There are many different ways to organize the same set of things.
Which perspective is taken is as important as which perspective is not taken.
Which distinctions are made are as important as which distinctions are not made.

variants.label: Draft A
variants.stem: Which of the following are true?

choices.text: What is left unrelated matters as much as what is related.
The same set of things can be organized in many ways.
The perspective not taken matters as much as the perspective taken.
The distinctions not made matter as much as the distinctions made.

variants.label: Draft B
variants.stem: Which of the following are true?

choices.text: The relationships you do not draw are part of the analysis.
One collection of parts can be grouped in more than one way.
Choosing a point of view also chooses which points of view to leave out.
Naming one thing also leaves other things unnamed.

variants.label: Draft C
variants.stem: Which of the following are true?

choices.text: Seeing what is not connected is as useful as seeing what is connected.
There is more than one valid way to organize the same parts.
A perspective includes the perspectives it sets aside.
A distinction includes the other it sets aside.

variants.label: Original
variants.stem: Which of the following are true?

choices.text: When some thing is not recognized, neither is its perspective.
Any thing or idea can be a perspective.
Perspectives can be made up of parts, which are themselves perspectives.

variants.label: Draft A
variants.stem: Which of the following are true?

choices.text: If something is not recognized, its perspective is not recognized either.
Any thing or idea can serve as a perspective.
A perspective can have parts, and those parts can be perspectives.

variants.label: Draft B
variants.stem: Which of the following are true?

choices.text: An unseen thing brings no point of view with it.
Perspectives are not limited to people.
Perspectives can be broken into smaller perspectives.

variants.label: Draft C
variants.stem: Which of the following are true?

choices.text: Failing to distinguish something also fails to take its perspective.
A tool, a rule, or a place can be a perspective.
The parts of a perspective are themselves points of view.

related parts of a system grouped according to a particular perspective
the only way to organize information
